records.label: spacr.qt.screens.embeddings#3
records.source: **What it is for.** Giving every object a vector that no label went into. The measured panel says how big a cell is and how bright each stain was; an embedding says what the cell LOOKS like, in a few hundred numbers a pretrained backbone produces without being told what to look for. That is what makes it worth having beside the panel rather than instead of it -- a phenotype nobody thought to measure is in the vector, and is in no column.
records.context: **What it is for.** Giving every object a vector that no label went into. The measured panel says how big a cell is and how bright each stain was; an embedding says what the cell LOOKS like, in a few hundred numbers a pretrained backbone produces without being told what to look for. That is what makes it worth having beside the panel rather than instead of it -- a phenotype nobody thought to measure is in the vector, and is in no column.
records.translation: **用途。** 为每个对象提供一个不含任何标签信息的向量。测量面板说明了细胞有多大、每种染色有多亮；嵌入向量则说明细胞看起来是什么样子，用的是预训练骨干网络在没有被告知要看什么的情况下生成的几百个数字。这正是它值得与面板并列存在、而不是取代面板的原因——没有人想到去测量的表型，会存在于向量中，而不存在于任何一列中。
records.review_basis: written from the English (no current MT draft)

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.embeddings#4
records.source: **What it needs.** Crops, and a choice about the channels. The crops come from the row at the top of the screen, which is :mod:`spacr.crop_loader`: either a ``measurements.db``, narrowed to one object class, one plate or any condition its crop table supports, or a folder of crop PNGs. Whichever it is, the pixels are read the way every other screen reads them -- :func:`spacr.crops.resolve_crop_source` decides between the crops already under ``data/`` and cutting them from ``merged/*.npy``, and says which it chose. Nothing has to be prepared first: a plate that has been through Measure with crop output on is ready.
records.context: **What it needs.** Extracted image regions, and a choice about the channels. The extracted image regions come from the row at the top of the application view, which is :mod:`spacr.crop_loader`: either a ``measurements.db``, narrowed to one object class, one laboratory microplate or any condition its extracted-image-region table supports, or a folder of extracted image region PNGs. records.label: spacr.qt.settings_search.SettingsSearchBar.reveal#3
records.source: THE DISCLOSURE LEVEL IS CHANGED ONLY IF IT HAS TO BE, AND THE CHANGE IS NEVER REMEMBERED. Switching to All settings unconditionally would work, and it would also rewrite this module's remembered Essentials/All choice every time anybody arrived here -- a setting the user chose, changed as a side effect of looking something up. So the filter is cleared first and the level is raised only when the row is still not on the form afterwards, which is exactly the case where Essentials is what is hiding it; and the raise goes through :meth:`_show_all_without_remembering`, so the form shows the row while the store still holds the level the user picked. Most settings are not essentials, so a lookup that persisted the raise would move almost every module out of Essentials for good.

records.label: spacr.qt.sound#4
records.source: **Qt Multimedia is touched only on the GUI thread.** :class:`_SoundPlayer` owns ``QMediaDevices`` and every ``QSoundEffect`` and lives where the application's event loop does; the dedicated ``QThread`` keeps the part that is genuinely slow, which is synthesizing a sound set (:class:`_SoundRenderer`, numpy and file writes, nothing from Qt Multimedia). Connecting to the sound server is slow -- 354 ms measured on a PipeWire workstation -- so it is paid ONCE, on an idle timer after sound is switched on (:meth:`SoundEngine._warm`), and logged rather than felt. Playing an already loaded sound is ``play()``, which returns at once: 0.007-0.014 ms on the GUI thread against the real stack.
records.context: **Qt Multimedia is touched only on the main GUI execution path.** :class:`_SoundPlayer` owns ``QMediaDevices`` and every ``QSoundEffect`` and lives where the application's event loop does; the dedicated ``QThread`` keeps the part that is genuinely slow, which is synthesizing a sound set (:class:`_SoundRenderer`, numpy and file writes, nothing from Qt Multimedia). Connecting to the sound server is slow -- 354 ms measured on a PipeWire workstation -- so it is paid ONCE, on an idle timer after sound is switched on (:meth:`SoundEngine._warm`), and logged rather than felt. records.translation: **只在 GUI 线程上接触 Qt Multimedia。** :class:`_SoundPlayer` 拥有 ``QMediaDevices`` 和每个 ``QSoundEffect``，并位于应用程序事件循环所在的线程；专用的 ``QThread`` 负责真正耗时的部分，即合成一套声音（:class:`_SoundRenderer`、numpy 和文件写入，不涉及 Qt Multimedia 的任何内容）。连接声音服务器很慢 -- 在一台 PipeWire 工作站上实测为 354 ms -- 因此这一开销只付出一次，在打开声音后由空闲计时器执行（:meth:`SoundEngine._warm`），并记录到日志中，而不会让用户感觉到。播放已加载的声音就是调用 ``play()``，它会立即返回：在真实音频栈上，于 GUI 线程中耗时 0.007-0.014 ms。

records.context: This rule is written in a crash.
